nodes.question: What equipment was used to control and record the tank temperature during the experiments?
nodes.answer: Apex aquarium controllers were used to control the temperature, and Hobo Pendant loggers were used to record the temperature every 15 minutes.
nodes.paragraph: 2022). Montipora capitata in K ne ohe Bay harbors Cladocopium and Durusdinium (Cunning et al. 2017), and here, symbiont community was summarized by genus. Collections In early November 2017, one fragment (~ 20 cm3) was col-lected from each of 5 tagged colonies at each study site to represent the patch reef population. Using genotype assign- ments (Caruso and Rocha de Souza et al. 2022), we detected 5 clonal pairs and one triplet and selected one sample of 401 Coral Reefs (2025) 44:399 409 each to yield a set of unique coral genotypes for final analy - sis. To assess genotype effects, we also collected 25 repli- cate fragments from 8 unique M. capitata genotypes from two previously established study sites (Barott et al. 2021). All fragments were glued on labeled aragonite plugs and acclimated to laboratory conditions for 12 weeks in outdoor seawater tables (Fig. 1B). Experimental temperature profiles We distributed fragments haphazardly into 10 indoor flow- through tanks (40 L) in late January 2018. Tank temperature was controlled with Apex aquarium controllers (Neptune Systems), and temperature was recorded on Hobo Pendant loggers (Onset Computer Corp) every 15 min.
